profile.name: Luigi Scofano de Araujo
profile.headline: Curiosity in code.
profile.intro: I am an undergraduate Computer Engineering student at Poli-USP. I explore artificial intelligence and data by building applications, experiments, and tools that turn ideas into something tangible.
about: I enjoy understanding how things work: how an algorithm chooses a move, how an image becomes information, and how to organize data without losing its context.
My path connects academic research, software development, and data analysis. I am currently deepening my studies in machine learning, generative AI, and data engineering.
I am also a jiu-jitsu instructor. Teaching is part of how I approach my projects: clear explanations, practice, and room to learn through experimentation.
profile.photoAlt: Luigi Scofano in a seaside landscape, with a small pixel-art great kiskadee in the photo
aboutOverview: I am Luigi Scofano de Araujo, a Computer Engineering student at Poli-USP. I am interested in artificial intelligence and data, especially in understanding how algorithms work and turning that knowledge into applications that other people can use and explore. I enjoy investigating how a program chooses a move, how an image can become information, and how to organize data without losing the context of where it came from.

In my undergraduate research at IME-USP, I study natural language processing and optical character recognition applied to Tupi Antigo, under the supervision of Professor Marcelo Finger. I work on organizing and reviewing data from historical sources, preserving the original spelling and the context of the information. This means looking beyond the extracted text: recording its source, identifying possible errors, and distinguishing what the software suggests from what still needs review. I also contribute to a virtual museum of computing at LASSu-USP, a laboratory coordinated by Professor Tereza Cristina Melo de Brito Carvalho.

This curiosity takes different forms in my projects. In Intuição, I develop logic and strategy games that let people explore decisions and how algorithms work. In GestureLab, I work with computer vision to experiment with interactions using hands, gestures, and poses captured by a webcam. In Pokédex, the focus is on organizing data and creating an interface for exploring species, forms, and evolutions. These are different projects, but they all give me room to study, test ideas, and pay attention to how people experience them.

My experience also includes data analysis and academic group projects, including digital circuits and FPGA applications. Across software, data, and hardware, I try to understand both the parts of a system and how they connect.
Outside computing, I am a jiu-jitsu instructor. Teaching is also part of how I approach my projects: explaining clearly, encouraging practice, and leaving room to learn through experimentation.

projects.name: Intuição
projects.subtitle: Learning through discovery
projects.type: Independent project · Classical AI and games
projects.summary: Logic, geometry, and strategy games that turn concepts into visible decisions. The AI calculates its moves directly in the browser.
projects.details: A platform with 11 games: eight solo campaigns and three Versus games. DESVIO uses exact search with memoization on supported maps; CERCO combines minimax, alpha-beta pruning, and heuristics.
projects.contribution: Development of mechanics, levels, interface, hints, and documentation. The repository distinguishes original code, visual assets, and third-party credits.
projects.limitation: Classical game AI, with no generative model. CERCO uses a bounded search and does not guarantee perfect play; BROTO is a two-player duel, with no bot in this version.
projects.imageAlt: Actual CERCO game board from Intuição, with two teams of animals and a barrier
projects.caption: CERCO · Application screenshot from the repository

projects.name: Undergraduate Research · Tupi Antigo
projects.subtitle: From historical source to data
projects.summary: Tools for structuring and reviewing lexicographic data while preserving sources, original spelling, and human review decisions.
projects.details: A TSV pipeline for importing, NFC normalization, auditing, and exporting, with CER/WER metrics and optional OCR via Tesseract. Research supervised by Professor Marcelo Finger, PhD.
projects.contribution: Research and tools documented by Luigi. The documentation acknowledges the academic partnership with Calebe Rezende’s Dicionário Tupi-Português.
projects.limitation: The demo uses fictional records. The repository does not distribute the complete validated corpus or provide automatic sentence translation.

projects.name: Kaggle-oRF
projects.subtitle: Decisions in different directions
projects.summary: An oblique decision forest implementation for investigating boundaries that combine multiple features at each node.
projects.details: Coursework for PCS 3838, Artificial Intelligence, at Poli-USP. Includes orthogonal and oblique trees, forests, and prediction export. Each node learns its directions through PCA/SVD and selects splits based on information gain.
projects.contribution: A collaborative academic project. The implementation and contribution history are available in the repository; it is not presented as solely authored work.
projects.limitation: A demonstration using synthetic data. No score, Kaggle ranking, or experimental competition results are presented. The figure is educational, not a benchmark.
projects.imageAlt: Educational figure comparing orthogonal and oblique splits across points from two classes
projects.caption: Educational illustration from the repository · Not an experimental result

projects.name: GestureLab
projects.subtitle: Movement as an interface
projects.summary: A webcam-based lab for tracking hands, recognizing gestures, drawing in the air, and comparing poses with a local catalog.
projects.details: Four independent modes: hands, gestures, airwrite, and posematch. The application connects detected coordinates to interaction states, stroke smoothing, export, and geometric comparison.
projects.contribution: Integration, interaction logic, local interface, geometric descriptor, reproducible catalog, and tests. The detection models are pretrained MediaPipe models.
projects.limitation: No custom models are trained, and air writing does not include word recognition. The pose preview uses synthetic input and does not represent a performance measurement.
projects.imageAlt: Synthetic PoseMatch preview showing a pose and the catalog reference
projects.caption: PoseMatch · Demonstration with synthetic input

projects.name: Pokédex
projects.subtitle: Data to explore
projects.summary: An interface for exploring species, forms, evolutions, and game-specific information, with versioned data and reproducible imports.
projects.details: A searchable catalog with filters, browser-stored favorites, Shiny mode, stats, and evolution families. The original Java exercise remains in a separate module.
projects.contribution: A fan application developed by Luigi, with a responsive interface, data preparation, tests, and documentation. Sources for data and images are identified in the repository.
projects.limitation: Queries reflect the coverage of the imported dataset. Favorites are stored in the browser. Pokémon and its assets belong to their respective rights holders; this is an unofficial project.
projects.imageAlt: Actual home page of Luigi’s Pokédex, featuring the species catalog
projects.caption: Actual application screenshot · Documented version 1.3.2

projects.name: Digital Laboratory
projects.subtitle: From code to circuit
projects.summary: FPGA circuits and games that connect state machines, sensors, serial communication, and computer interfaces.
projects.details: A collection from Poli-USP’s Digital Laboratory I and II courses, with experiments and the Math Genius and Guardião do Paredão projects. Includes source files, reports, simulations, and verification tools.
projects.contribution: Group projects, with authorship, teaching materials, and subsequent organization identified in the repository’s implementation documentation.
projects.limitation: Simulation and compilation are not equivalent to hardware validation. Physical validation of the revisions in this edition remains pending; no claims of therapeutic effectiveness are made.
